My point estimates reflect a relatively stable but gently upward-drifting baseline from what I understood to be a current gold price in the neighborhood of $1,720–$1,730 per troy ounce. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of $1,732 is essentially an anchoring to recent price levels with minimal expected drift, since intraday and overnight moves in gold tend to be small absent a major catalyst. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to $1,738, reflecting a mild positive drift assumption consistent with modest safe-haven demand and a soft-dollar environment that has characterized recent months. The one-month estimate of $1,750 continues that gentle upward trajectory, incorporating a view that real interest rates, while elevated, may not rise dramatically further in the near term, leaving some room for gold to appreciate modestly.

The confidence interval widths expand predictably with time horizon, reflecting the compounding of daily uncertainty. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly ±39 points captures typical overnight volatility in gold, which historically runs in the range of 0.5–1.5% on an annualized basis translated to daily moves. By one week, the interval widens to ±70 points to account for the possibility of Fed communication, inflation data releases, or geopolitical developments shifting sentiment. By one month, the interval of ±140 points reflects the full range of macro surprises that could materialize — including shifts in monetary policy expectations, dollar strength, and risk appetite — all of which are meaningful drivers of gold over a four-week window.

There are several tail risks that could push gold well outside my stated intervals. On the upside, an unexpected escalation in geopolitical conflict, a sharp equity market selloff, or a sudden pivot in Fed rhetoric toward cutting rates could send gold through the top of the one-month interval and potentially toward $1,950 or higher. Conversely, a materially stronger-than-expected jobs report or inflation reading that cements expectations for further aggressive rate hikes could strengthen the dollar and pressure gold below $1,600, breaking the lower bound of the one-month interval. Liquidity events or a sudden risk-on rally in equities draining safe-haven demand represent additional downside risks that are hard to quantify precisely but are real.

It is also worth noting that my forecast was made without real-time market data, so there is inherent model uncertainty in where exactly prices stood at the time of forecasting.
